Every averaged zero-error effect therefore has form tq|wbq⟩⟨wbq|. Its normalization requires tq P x p−1 q−x|x, q −x⟩⟨x, q −x| ≤I, so tq ≤minx pq−x, which is attainable. A block with fewer than N terms cannot give positive symmetric zero-error success: otherwise all N vectors would be linearly independent, since applying their zero-error effects to a linear relation isolates each coefficient. There are fewer than N available dimensions. Thus the exact optimal average success is η(r) = X q min 0≤x<N pq−x. (25)
